rest.notification.answers.malformed: Any endpoint, when the body is not JSON, lacks a field the endpoint requires, or carries one of those fields as something other than a string. The body is read as JSON whatever `Content-Type` says, and fields the endpoint does not take are ignored. Checked after the token and the size.
rest.notification.answers.unauthenticate: Any endpoint, when the token Kong let through fails notification's own check: an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer` followed by the token (Kong finds the token after the word `Bearer` anywhere in the header), a token that is not an access token (a refresh token or a two-factor challenge token), one issued for another audience, one without `sub`, `exp`, `iat` or `jti`, or a `sub` longer than 64 characters. Refresh the access token or sign in again, then repeat the request.
rest.notification.answers.notFound: Any path under `/api/v1/notifications/devices` other than the two served, a trailing slash included.
rest.notification.answers.methodNotAllow: A served path asked with a method it does not take. Through Kong that is `DELETE` or `OPTIONS` on `/api/v1/notifications/devices/verify`, or an `OPTIONS` on `/api/v1/notifications/devices` that Kong did not answer as a CORS preflight. `Allow` lists the methods the path takes: `POST` for `/verify`, `POST, DELETE` for the other.
rest.notification.answers.tooLarge: Any endpoint, when the body is longer than 4,096 bytes. Checked after the token, before the body is parsed.
rest.notification.answers.internal: Any endpoint, when something fails that notification did not expect. The answer has no body, and whether the request took effect is unknown. Registering and forgetting are safe to repeat; after a failed verification, register again: `200` means the token is already the caller's.
rest.notification.answers.database: Any endpoint, when notification cannot read or write its device registry. `message` names the store; why it failed is only in notification's log. Nothing can be said about what the request would have done; retry later. Registering and forgetting are safe to repeat.
rest.notification.answers.keysUnreadable: Any endpoint, when notification cannot read identity's signing keys to check the token. This says nothing about the token: keep it and retry later, without signing in again.
rest.notification.registerDevice.summary: Registers this handset's FCM token, so that push notifications for the signed-in principal reach it. A token held by nobody, or already held by the caller, is registered at once. A token another principal holds is moved only after the handset proves possession through `POST /api/v1/notifications/devices/verify`: one proof at a time per claimant, and at most 3 an hour per token. A principal keeps at most 10 handsets: registering one more forgets the handset registered least recently, rather than refusing the new one.
rest.notification.registerDevice.who: Any signed-in principal: customer, seller, courier or admin; no role is checked. The token is bound to the principal the access token names (`sub`). A `principal_id`, or any other field the body adds, is ignored.
rest.notification.registerDevice.field.d: The handset's FCM registration token. Whitespace around it is trimmed; 1 to 512 characters must remain.
rest.notification.registerDevice.field.p: `ANDROID` or `IOS`, in capitals. Whitespace around it is trimmed; any other value is refused.
rest.notification.registerDevice.case.ad: The token was held by nobody and is now the caller's. If the caller now holds more than 10 handsets, those registered least recently are forgotten in the same transaction.
rest.notification.registerDevice.case.re: The caller already held this token. Its `platform` and registration time are updated, so this handset becomes the most recently registered; an app can register at every start without losing its place.
rest.notification.registerDevice.case.ve: Another principal holds this token, and nothing moved. The handset was sent an FCM data message with `kind` `DEVICE_VERIFICATION`, a `nonce` and `expires_at`, 10 minutes from now. The app must read that message and send the `nonce` to `POST /api/v1/notifications/devices/verify` with an access token for the same principal before `expires_at`. Until then, the same principal registering this token again gets `429` `VERIFICATION_ALREADY_PENDING` and nothing is sent; if the data message never arrives, register again after `expires_at`.
rest.notification.registerDevice.case.in: `device_token` is empty after trimming, or longer than 512 characters. Checked before `platform`.
`platform` is neither `ANDROID` nor `IOS`; the comparison is case-sensitive, so `android` is refused.
rest.notification.registerDevice.case.ad: Another principal holds this token, and FCM answered the proof message that the token no longer exists (`UNREGISTERED`, or `INVALID_ARGUMENT` about the token itself). Notification forgets the token for whoever held it, and no proof is pending. Get a fresh FCM token on the handset and register that one: nobody holds it, so it is registered at once.
rest.notification.registerDevice.case.fo: Another principal holds this token, and FCM answered the proof message that the token belongs to another app (`SENDER_ID_MISMATCH`). `error` is the same as in the case above; `message` differs. The token is not forgotten: its holder keeps it, and no proof is pending or counted. Get an FCM token from Kinetix's own app on the handset and register that one.
rest.notification.registerDevice.case.al: Another principal holds this token, and a proof sent for it to this caller has not expired yet, so nothing is sent again. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until that proof expires, and `message` names the moment. Send the `nonce` the handset already received to `POST /api/v1/notifications/devices/verify`; register again after `Retry-After` only if the data message never arrived.
rest.notification.registerDevice.case.li: Another principal holds this token, and it has been sent 3 proofs in the last hour, whoever claimed it; a proof FCM did not take is not counted. Nothing is sent. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the oldest of those three is an hour old, and `message` names that moment: register again then. Pushes keep going to the current holder meanwhile.
rest.notification.registerDevice.case.se: Another principal holds this token, and FCM refused the proof message for a reason that concerns neither the token, nor how much notification may send, nor notification's own credentials. No proof is pending and nothing was counted; what FCM said is only in notification's log. Sending the same request again does not help.

Another principal holds this token, and FCM did not take the proof message: 3 attempts were made, and the last got no answer or a server error. No proof is pending and nothing was counted against the 3 an hour, so a retry later is safe.

Another principal holds this token, and FCM did not take the proof message: 3 attempts were made, and the last was refused because notification is sending more than FCM allows (`429`). `Retry-After` is the wait FCM named with its refusal, in whole seconds, from 1 to 3,600; 60 when it named none that notification can read. No proof is pending and nothing was counted against the 3 an hour: register again after `Retry-After`.

Another principal holds this token, and FCM did not accept notification's own credentials (`401` or `403`, other than for a token of another app). Neither the request nor the handset is at fault; no proof is pending and nothing was counted. The answer carries no `Retry-After`; retry later. When FCM refuses notification's Google access token, notification renews it and sends the message once more first, so a credential that has merely expired does not cause this answer.
rest.notification.verifyDevice.summary: Completes a move that `POST /api/v1/notifications/devices` answered with `202`: the caller sends the nonce its handset received, and the token becomes the caller's.
rest.notification.verifyDevice.who: The principal that received the `202`, with an access token naming the same principal (`sub`). The nonce proves only that principal's claim; the current holder sending it moves nothing.
rest.notification.verifyDevice.field.dev: The FCM registration token the `202` was given for. Trimmed; 1 to 512 characters.
rest.notification.verifyDevice.field.non: The `nonce` from the `DEVICE_VERIFICATION` data message the handset received, unchanged. Trimmed; 1 to 128 characters.
rest.notification.verifyDevice.case.veri: The nonce matches the latest one sent for this caller and token, and has not expired. The token now belongs to the caller, the nonce cannot be used again, and the limit of 10 handsets is applied as on registration.
rest.notification.verifyDevice.case.inva: `device_token` is empty after trimming, or longer than 512 characters. Checked before `nonce`.
`nonce` is empty after trimming, or longer than 128 characters.
rest.notification.verifyDevice.case.notP: No proof is pending for this caller and this token: none was started, it was already used, it expired, or five wrong nonces spent it. Register the device again to have a new nonce sent; a token is sent at most 3 proofs an hour.
rest.notification.verifyDevice.case.nonc: The nonce is not the one sent to the handset. `message` says how many attempts are left; the fifth miss spends the proof, and the next attempt answers `VERIFICATION_NOT_PENDING`.
rest.notification.forgetDevice.summary: Stops push notifications to a handset by forgetting its FCM token, if the signed-in principal holds it. Send it when the user signs out on that handset.
rest.notification.forgetDevice.who: Any signed-in principal, for its own handsets only.
rest.notification.forgetDevice.field.dev: The FCM registration token to forget. Trimmed; 1 to 512 characters.
rest.notification.forgetDevice.case.forg: The same answer whether the token was the caller's and is now forgotten, belongs to another principal and was left alone, or was not registered at all. Safe to repeat.
rest.notification.forgetDevice.case.inva: `device_token` is empty after trimming, or longer than 512 characters.
